Abyss Manager Idle is a game that deserves a sequel or enhanced release. This is a semi-idle tower defense/incremental game. The developer was pretty transparent up front that this would be a shorter experience, and that the game would be free. However, I found myself enjoying the game a lot more than expected, especially on the depth side. Sure things are a bit compressed and the game is short (I finished in 2.5 hours or so), but with a redesign the progression could be smoother. Additionally, there are parts of the progression that feel like they had not been fully hashed out yet, leaving me wanting more. I came out of this game feeling more like I just played a pretty entertaining demo that I enjoyed. Overall, this game is honestly pretty fun for the 2-3 hours of gameplay there is (also easy 100% achievements). I wish they would release a longer/fuller version of the game in the future, as this has a lot of potential.

As far as free games go, this has been a fantastic waste of time. The economy needs a lot more work as it's pretty easy to run out of things to spend money on long before you run out of things to do and the red mana feels absolutely useless after a certain point. Many of the power ups feel exactly the same, just under a slightly different mechanic. It's a good game with really cute art, though and it's been a pleasant way to relax in-between tasks. Hope to see the developer return to working on it soon.

Pretty dang fun, although it has it's flaws. This is definitely not your average idler, it's a bizarre (but great) mash-up of your standard incremental idler, and tower defense, with some RPG elements thrown in. There are many characters to unlock, and they're all different, and on top of that, the sprite work is pretty fantastic. It was fun trying to unlock all of them. Now to complain a bit. While there are info windows for each panel that you open up, the game does [i]not[/i] do a fantastic job of explaining what everything is/does, and even what your main goal is, or how to go about it. There was a LOT of blind trial and error trying to figure out what everything was, but that was kind of part of the fun. I hate to say this, but a little more hand-holding would have gone a long way here. It gets to the point where most of the panels that you have unlocked become totally ignorable, since everything has a maximum level that you can get, and that includes character levels, and any and all upgrades that you can purchase. My main gripe is the fact that there doesn't seem to be any kind of threat at ALL here, if you let the enemies through, you never fail. You can't lose. The TD aspect of the game is diminished a ton when you can literally let 100% of the enemies through and just keep playing. Yeah, I complained a bit there, but this game is definitely worth playing. For FREE, I got almost 4 hours out of it. If you like incrementals and/or TD's, and have a few hours, give this one a go. If it had more content, this could easily be a game worth a few dollars.
